evidence.claim: Fewer than 1% of day traders outperform consistently; about 13% profitable in a typical year (Taiwan)
evidence.quote: While about 13% earn profits net of fees in the typical year, the results of our analysis suggest that less than 1% of day traders (1,000 out of 360,000) are able to outperform consistently.
evidence.source: Barber, Lee, Liu, Odean, The Cross-Section of Speculator Skill: Evidence from Day Trading, draft 2011; J. Financial Markets 18 (2014) 1-24

evidence.claim: Top day traders' gross returns do not survive costs
evidence.quote: In aggregate, they earn positive gross returns on their day trading of 13.1 basis points per day (t=17.28), but these profits do not survive costs, and active day traders lose about 6.8 basis points per day net of fees (t=-9.02).

evidence.claim: 97% of Brazilian mini-index futures day traders persisting 300+ days lost money; no learning
evidence.quote: We observe all individuals who began to day trade between 2013 and 2015 in the Brazilian equity futures market, the third in terms of volume in the world, and persisted for at least 300 days: 97% of them lost money, only 0.4% earned more than a bank teller (US$54 per day), and the top individual earned only US$310 per day with great risk (a standard deviation of US$2,560). Additionally, we find no evidence of learning by day trading.
evidence.source: Chague, De-Losso, Giovannetti (2019), Day Trading for a Living?, FEA-USP WP 2019-47 / FGV EESP TD 525 / SSRN 3423101

evidence.claim: Crossing stop-loss clusters (round numbers) gives faster continuation, not reversal
evidence.quote: For example, dollar-mark moves an average 0.061 percent during the 15 minutes after crossing a round number, but only 0.054 percent after crossing an arbitrary number. Since the average move is higher for round numbers than for arbitrary numbers in 51 of the 58 relevant 10-day intervals, marginal significance for this test is below 0.001 percent.
evidence.source: Osler (2002), Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets, FRBNY Staff Report 150

evidence.claim: Pointer: open-based ORB on futures changed after 24-h electronic trading
evidence.quote: What I can tell you is that in the old Pit days "Open" worked well across many markets. Now in 24hr e-trading, Close at a bigger spread and (High+Low+Close)/3 work well in different markets.
